verdict: The revision fixes the prior authorization findings it names (S9/S10 scoped to non-authority authors, A5's backup-replacement clause, keyed genesis admission, S1 gating of stages, the explicit escalation ladder, the durable rotation worker, freeze under the lock, Delete under the freeze, the pins Secret and resetPins). What it introduced collides with the flows it was meant to protect: G6 now applies to recovery records, so the hijack recovery (restore kicked victims + remove the rogue) is refused and serialized recoveries are defeated because an accepted recovery clears the freeze; a RemoveIdentity on a frozen group sets needs_rotation while the rotating half is deferred, and 6.4's export precondition (needs_rotation = false) can then never be met, so the bundle the spec says to re-export cannot be exported; the OpenStage write fence is granted to any bit-holder and to any registered identity presenting any historical recovery record (the gate checks only C3), so a reader, a write-only CI key or a kicked identity can hold a group write-fenced indefinitely; S9 exempts rotates and S4's straggler service re-encrypts up to 16 MiB under the global lock for a rotate with an empty stage, so any admin can churn heads for free and hold the bunker-wide lock at will; and a lost (not merely compromised) operational key leaves a server that refuses to start and a recovery that needs a running server, a regression from today's offline `recover`. The remainder are single-sentence gaps: S5 not binding the record's wraps to the stage's, the recovery gate placed on StageVersions vs OpenStage, S7's rationale and `db remove-identity`, registrable authority keys bypassing S9/S10, the S5 key for an authority-replacing recovery, legacy Grant under a freeze, pin-Secret lag, and the sole-service-admin rogue. Full report: /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-dragan-fables-for-robots-secret-bunker-iroh/0c07f4bd-a1ff-4066-aa31-2b8de0a5ded7/scratchpad/review3/authz.json

unfixed_prior.prior_title: G6 still admits the one-id stale resubmission it was written for
unfixed_prior.why_not_fixed: G6 now defines a revived id (in an earlier record, absent from head.acl) and constrains records that add one to a sole change. The accidental case the rule was written against is exactly a sole change: head h = {alice: rwa, bob: rwa, dave: r}; alice builds a repair rewrap against h; bob's rotate h+1 kicks dave; a non-compliant client rebuilds alice's record against h+1 with its stale ACL (wraps to M_new from alice's wrap in h+1): delta = {+dave}, a sole revival, accepted by every verifier and attributed to alice. The revision declares this 'deliberate' (G6: 'Revival is deliberate, never accidental') but no field in the record distinguishes deliberate from stale; only the 6.2 client rule does.
unfixed_prior.fix: Either state in G6/7.4 that the sole-revival case is a client-side residual (the 6.2 delta rule plus the EpochConflict diff) and that G6 catches only multi-change resubmissions, or add a per-entry revive marker (a perms bit 0x08 'revived', set by the client only when the user named the id explicitly; a record adding a revived id without the bit is refused, the bit is cleared on install so it never persists in head.acl).

unfixed_prior.prior_title: An online kick target starves the client-signed kick (rotates unlimited)
unfixed_prior.why_not_fixed: The ladder is now explicit, but S9 still bounds only non-rotating records, and S4's straggler service makes a rotate with an empty staged set cost the rogue two small messages while the server re-encrypts up to 16 MiB for it and the kicker restarts at step 2 (full export + re-encrypt) after every one, since the CLI refuses to rebase over a target-authored record. Rung 1 is therefore never reachable against a target that rotates; see the S9 finding for the server-side cost that makes this bunker-wide rather than per-kick.
unfixed_prior.fix: Count rotating records in S9 (e.g. at most 1 accepted rotate per non-authority author per group per 60 s) and make stragglers cost the author (see finding).

findings.section: 5 G6 vs 6.4 (recovery), S10 ('an accepted recovery clears the freeze'), 13 e2e (7)
findings.title: G6 applies to recovery, so the hijack recovery is refused and serialized recoveries are re-hijacked between ceremonies
findings.detail: G6: 'A record of any kind whose ACL adds a revived id MUST make no other ACL change.' 6.4 trigger 1 is 'a rogue admin locked everyone out', i.e. the rogue R authored a rotate with acl = {R: rwa}; alice and bob now appear in earlier records but not in head.acl, so both are revived ids. The operator freezes, exports and runs `recovery author --acl alice:rwa bob:r` (with --rotate, R6, since R is removed): the record revives two ids and removes R -> refused 'G6' by the server, every replica and `client epoch log`. Serializing does not help: recovery 1 may only add alice (sole revival, R must stay: removing R is 'another ACL change', and acl = {} fails G2); it lands and 'An accepted recovery clears the freeze'; R is still an admin of the new head and online, so R rotates alice out again (A2, a few ms with a small group) before the operator can re-freeze; recovery 2 (remove R) then leaves no admin (G2) or must re-add alice (revival + removal, G6). The loop has no exit that the spec describes. A workaround exists but is unstated and not what the documented command produces: add a brand-new admin key (first-time id, unconstrained) and remove R in one recovery, then let that key re-add the victims one record each. 13 e2e (7) ('Recovery bundle for an orphaned group, with --rotate, against a rogue admin held off by FreezeGroup') written the natural way fails on G6. G6's purpose (stale-ACL resubmission) has no analogue for recoveries: a recovery is signed offline against an exported head and is never rebased automatically.
findings.fix: Exempt `recovery` from G6 ('G6 applies to rewrap, rotate and carry; a recovery's ACL is deliberate by construction, A4'). Independently, do not clear the freeze on a recovery unless the operator asked: `recovery author --unfreeze` sets a flag byte the install honours, otherwise the freeze stays until `FreezeGroup{frozen: false}`; state in 6.4 step 3 that the operator unfreezes after verifying the head with `client epoch log`. Add the server test: recovery reviving two ids and removing the rogue lands on a frozen group and the group stays frozen until unfrozen.

findings.section: 5 S10 and the 'Server-only' preamble vs 6.3 (rotating half 'defers a frozen group') vs 6.4 step 1 ('export only when frozen and needs_rotation = false')
findings.title: RemoveIdentity on a frozen group deadlocks the recovery ceremony: needs_rotation cannot clear while frozen and export requires it clear
findings.detail: S10: server-side revocation carries land on a frozen group; 'the rotating half is deferred while frozen'. 6.3: the worker 'defers a frozen group'. 6.4 step 1: 'export only when GroupStatus shows frozen and needs_rotation = false'. 6.4 later: 'A RemoveIdentity touching the group after the export moves the head; ... the bundle is re-exported and re-signed.' Sequence: operator runs `client freeze-group g` (rogue admin R online); a service admin runs RemoveIdentity(carol) (a reader of g, unrelated offboarding, or one of 'several admin keys [that] are suspect'); the carry lands on frozen g, needs_rotation := 1; the worker defers. The export precondition is now false and stays false for as long as the freeze holds, and the freeze is what the ceremony requires; the re-export the spec prescribes for exactly this event cannot happen. The only exit is an undocumented unfreeze (worker rotates in seconds, during which R may move the head again) followed by a re-freeze and a fresh export. The precondition is unnecessary: a recovery authored with --rotate has dek_gen = head + 1 and clears the flag on install (6.1 step 3), and a non-rotating recovery leaves the flag for the worker after the freeze clears. Separately, the Server-only preamble says 'authority-authored records and recoveries are never rate-limited or frozen out (6.3, 6.4)' while S10 and 6.3 defer the authority rotate on a frozen group: the two sentences cannot both hold.
findings.fix: Drop 'needs_rotation = false' from 6.4 step 1; replace with: 'if GroupStatus shows needs_rotation, author the recovery with --rotate (the recovery clears the flag); the bundle is otherwise unaffected'. Reconcile the preamble with S10: either 'the rotating half is deferred while frozen (the only authority record a freeze holds back)' in both places, or let the worker rotate frozen groups (a rotate cannot add anyone, A3) and remove the deferral. Add the server test: freeze, RemoveIdentity of a reader, export, recovery --rotate lands and clears both flag and freeze.

findings.title: The OpenStage write fence is available to any bit-holder and to any registered identity holding any past recovery record
findings.detail: 6.1: 'From OpenStage until the stage is submitted or expires, Put and Delete on the group answer Failed{rotation-pending}... A stage can be opened only by a caller S1 admits for the group, so the fence is not available to strangers; an admin who abuses it can already do worse.' S1 admits 'a caller holding any bit on the group', so a read-only identity (the k8s operator's key, a compromised reader) or a write-only CI key can OpenStage and never submit: 15 min idle TTL renewed by one small StageVersions, 6 h hard ceiling, then a new stage_id ('a second stage_id from the same submitter for the same group replaces the first') - an indefinite write denial on the group by a party that cannot author any record and could not otherwise do worse; after being kicked it can no longer renew, so the fence outlives the kick by up to 15 min. Second path, with no bit at all: S1 also admits a stage whose recovery 'verifies under head.backup (C3 evaluated first)'. C3 is a signature check, so every recovery record ever installed on the chain still verifies under head.backup while backup is unchanged; the chain is readable by every reader (GroupEpochs) and by a kicked identity up to its removal (6.5 grace), and the bundle itself is handed to 'any registered identity' to carry. Any registered identity that ever saw such a record can OpenStage the group forever, and by SubmitEpoch of that stale record learns EpochConflict{head_epoch, head_hash} (C2 fails after C3 passes) for a group it holds no bit on - the oracle S1 was rewritten to close.
findings.fix: OpenStage/StageVersions: admit the caller iff it holds the admin bit in head.acl (A2 is the only author that can use a stage), or the record it presents is a recovery that passes C1-C4 against the current head (chained on it, not merely signed); anything else answers the uniform Denied. Evaluate C2 before answering: a recovery that verifies under head.backup but does not chain on the head answers Denied to a caller with no bit, EpochConflict only to an admin. Let an admin's accepted rotate delete every other open stage on the group (as the server-authored rotate already does). Add tests: reader OpenStage -> Denied; stale recovery from a registered non-member -> Denied.

findings.section: 5 S9 (non-rotating only) and S4 (stragglers under the lock) / 6.1 server step 3 / 6.1 step 8
findings.title: Unlimited rotates plus server-side straggler re-encryption let any admin hold the global store lock and churn heads for free
findings.detail: S9 bounds 'non-rotating SubmitEpoch records' only; rotates are unbounded. S4: at commit, every retained row not covered by a staged row is a straggler, and in mode A 'stragglers up to 16 MiB of ciphertext per commit are re-encrypted by the server itself'; 6.1 server step 3 does this 'Under the lock, in one SQLite transaction'. R2 accepts the empty-set digest (4.3: 'never zero for a rotating record'). Sequence: an admin of any group with <= 16 MiB retained sends OpenStage + SubmitEpoch{rotate, reencrypted = digest(empty)} with no StageVersions: the record verifies (A2, A5, R3), S5 passes (the server opens its own wrap), and the server decrypts and re-encrypts every retained version and rewrites every secret_version row while holding the bunker-wide store mutex, then publishes Changed to every replica (which refetch the whole group, section 10). Nothing limits the rate: each such SubmitEpoch is two small messages and costs the server tens to hundreds of ms of lock hold plus 16 MiB of WAL. Every Get/Put on every group of the bunker stalls behind it, and the rotation worker with them. The same mechanism inverts S9's stated rationale for kicks: the target's rotate is cheaper than the kicker's rebase ('otherwise restart at step 2': a full export and re-encrypt), and 6.1 step 8 refuses to rebase over a target-authored record at all, so rung 1 of the ladder is starved at no cost to the target. Rejected submissions are also uncounted, so a bounded verify (~12 ms on a blocking thread per S8) can be requested without limit; that is minor by comparison.
findings.fix: Count rotating records in S9 (e.g. 'and at most 1 accepted rotating record per non-authority author per group per 60 s'). Make stragglers the author's cost: at OpenStage snapshot the set of retained (name, version) rows; at commit a straggler is only a row absent from that snapshot (written after the fence, which is what stragglers were defined for), and any snapshot row left uncovered answers StaleVersions{versions}; a rotate that stages nothing against a non-empty group is then refused, not serviced. State the straggler re-encryption budget per author per interval if the first rule is kept. Add the test: rotate with an empty stage on a non-empty group -> StaleVersions listing every row.

findings.title: A lost operational key has no recovery path: serve refuses to start while any head names it, and the only recovery is over the wire to a running server
findings.detail: 6.4: the two-key start needs `--previous-operational-key old.key` (the file); 'a start without --previous-operational-key is refused while any head names it'. Today Bunker::new refuses a key that differs from meta (src/server.rs:64-88, 'operational key does not match the one recorded in the database'), and the spec keeps that check on meta.operational_ed25519. Every group's head names the operational key (mode A). Sequence: the host holding operational.key dies (or the operator destroys the key on suspicion of compromise, the natural reaction the spec's own trigger invites); the database is restored from backup; `serve --operational-key new.key` is refused (heads name the old key, no --previous flag); `serve --operational-key new.key --previous-operational-key old.key` cannot be given (no file). The recovery that would move each group to new.key (`recovery author --authority <new> --rotate`, signed by the backup key, which holds a wrap in every record) is submitted over the wire by `client epoch submit` and needs the server running. No offline install path exists: `recover` (src/main.rs:103-866, which today needs only the backup key and the new public key, offline) is removed in 11. The outage is total and permanent for every group. Only loss, not compromise, is affected, and 6.4's trigger list omits loss.
findings.fix: Let `serve` start with an unavailable previous key: `--previous-operational-id <hex>` (public key only) satisfies the 'heads still name it' check; groups whose head names a key the server does not hold answer Failed{"authority key unavailable"} to Get/Put and are skipped by the rotation worker and S5 until a recovery lands (S2 already accepts either meta value). Alternatively keep an offline install path: `db submit-recovery --db --bundle g.recovery` runs the verifier and the install transaction against the file with the service stopped (the same code path as SubmitEpoch, no S1). Add 'operational key lost' to the 6.4 trigger list and a server test for it.

findings.section: 5 S5 (per-row checks at StageVersions vs wrap check at SubmitEpoch) / 6.1 steps 5-7 / 9 OpenStage.wraps
findings.title: S5 never binds the record's wrap set to the stage's: rows checked under DEK_stage can be installed under a record committing to a different M
findings.detail: S5: the per-row checks run at StageVersions 'against the current source row', with the new DEK 'derived from the record when the stage was opened with SubmitEpoch's record hash, or from M handed over the fence' (the OpenStage `wraps`); at SubmitEpoch the server 'opens its own wrap from that record and refuses unless KDF(M') reproduces dek_commit'. Nothing says the record's wraps/dek_commit must equal the stage's `wraps`. Sequence: admin opens a stage with wraps W1 (M1), stages every row re-encrypted under DEK(M1) (all per-row checks pass), then submits a rotate whose wraps W2 commit to M2 (internally consistent: S5's wrap check passes, R3 proof passes). S4 installs the staged rows under dek_gen+1 with the record W2 as the head: every reader and the server derive DEK(M2) and fail the AEAD on every version. An admin can already commit garbage (3.8), but D7 and 7.1 claim the mode-A server 'refuse[s] a re-key that would brick readers', and this one it accepts.
findings.fix: S5: 'SubmitEpoch refuses a rotating record whose wrap set and dek_commit are not byte-identical to the stage's `wraps` ("S5: stage wraps differ"); a client that must change the wrap set (EpochConflict rebase, step 8) re-opens the stage with the new wraps, and the server re-runs the per-row check on the staged rows it already holds'.

findings.section: 5 S1 ('first StageVersions carries a recovery') vs 9 (OpenStage{recovery}) vs 6.1 (fence starts at OpenStage) / 6.4 step 3
findings.title: The recovery admission is placed on StageVersions in S1 and 6.4 but on OpenStage in section 9; under S1's reading a non-member carrier cannot open the stage the recovery needs
findings.detail: S1: 'a stage is accepted from a caller holding any bit on the group, or whose first StageVersions carries a recovery record verifying under head.backup'. 6.4 step 3: 'the first StageVersions carries the recovery record, which admits the stage'. Section 9: `OpenStage{group, stage_id, wraps, recovery: bstr or null}` and `StageVersions{group, stage_id, versions}` (no recovery field); 6.1: the stage and the fence begin at OpenStage and the server needs `wraps` there to derive DEK_new for the per-row checks. A carrier with no bit on the group ('any registered identity', 6.4) sends OpenStage first; under S1 as worded it is not admitted (no bit, no StageVersions yet) and answers Denied, so the recovery flow cannot start. Under section 9's shape it works. One of the two is wrong.
findings.fix: S1 and 6.4 step 3: 'or whose OpenStage carries a recovery record that passes C1-C4 against the current head' (see the OpenStage finding for why C3 alone is insufficient); StageVersions and SubmitEpoch then resolve the stage by (group, connection EndpointId, stage_id) as 6.1 says.

findings.title: S7 guards a state a restored snapshot cannot produce, while the path that does produce it (offline `db remove-identity` on a migrated database) is unspecified and leaves the removed key authorized on every replica
findings.detail: S7: 'the rule guards a restored snapshot'. identity and group_epoch live in the same SQLite file, so a snapshot restores both consistently: a key is either registered and in the head, or removed and out of every head (6.3, same transaction). The state S7 describes (in a head ACL, not registered) arises from `db remove-identity --db --name` (11: 'offline removal, needed by migration step 1'), which on a v3 database is not stated to author the authority carries. After it: the authoritative node denies the key (identity lookup fails), but every replica's mirrored ACL is the verified head (P5: 'no separate deny list is needed'), so the k8s operator and standalone replicas keep serving the removed key; the head still wraps M to it; and the operator must know to run `db revoke-key` separately. The rotation worker never fires (no carry, no flag).
findings.fix: 11/S7: `db remove-identity` on a database with epochs_migrated authors the same authority carries as RemoveIdentity (needs --operational-key) and sets needs_rotation, or refuses with 'use RemoveIdentity or db revoke-key'; `db revoke-key` deletes the identity row in the same transaction. Reword S7's rationale to name the offline-edit path. Both commands refuse to run while the server holds the file (in-memory head/seen sets would diverge).

findings.section: 5 S7 (pinned keys no longer refused at AddIdentity) / S1 / A3 / S9-S10 exemption
findings.title: The operational key can be registered as an identity and then submit S9/S10-exempt shrink records over the wire
findings.detail: The previous S7 refused registering a key equal to a configured pinned key; the revision's S7 refuses only ids in a head ACL, and pinned ids never appear in an ACL. D8 makes operational.key an iroh secret-key file, so `client --key operational.key` connects with EndpointId == authority. Sequence: a service admin (or the attacker who is one) registers the authority's public key; the holder of a stolen operational key connects as it and submits carry/rotate records with author == authority: S1 (connection id == author) passes, A3 admits shrink-only records, and the preamble exempts them from S9 and S10, so they land on frozen groups at any rate. Every offline recovery bundle (including the ones that replace this very key) then fails C2 on submission, indefinitely; 7.4 already grants the compromised key denial power, but the freeze was introduced so an offline recovery can land against an online churner, and this churner is immune to it. Requires a colluding service admin, hence minor.
findings.fix: S7: 'AddIdentity refuses meta.operational_ed25519, meta.operational_ed25519_previous and backup_ed25519'. S1: 'a wire SubmitEpoch whose author is the authority is refused (authority records are minted only by the server process)'. Optionally, S10 exempts only the server-minted revocation carry and the worker, not any record with author == authority.

findings.section: 6.4 'Operational-key replacement' ('S5 ... the key the group's head names') / 5 S2 / 6.4 'Backup replacement' ('or the authority rotates')
findings.title: S5 on an authority-replacing recovery must open the record's wrap with the new key, and the post-replacement 'authority rotates once more' has no trigger
findings.detail: 6.4: 'server-authored records on a group are signed by, and open wraps with, the key the group's head names; read_secret, S5 and straggler re-encryption do the same.' For the recovery `--authority <new id> --rotate` the head names the old key while the record's only server wrap is addressed to the new key; S5 as worded opens with the head's key, fails, and refuses the record that ends the two-key window - for every group, so the window never closes and the old key can never be dropped. Separately, 6.4's backup replacement says 'when the old key is suspect, any admin (or the authority) rotates once more afterwards': the worker rotates only groups with needs_rotation = 1, legacy RotateDek answers Failed, and nothing sets the flag on a backup replacement, so the authority variant does not exist.
findings.fix: S5/6.4: 'for a recovery, S5 opens the wrap addressed to the record's authority (either meta value, S2); for every other record, the head's'. Either drop '(or the authority)' or have `recovery author --backup <id>` set a flag byte that the install turns into needs_rotation := 1 so the worker performs the follow-up rotate.

findings.section: 5 S10 (legacy Grant refused while frozen) vs 6.3 (legacy shrink Grant is the server-side revocation, which 'still lands') / 6.1 ladder rung 2
findings.title: Legacy shrink Grant is both refused and landed on a frozen group
findings.detail: S10 lists 'legacy Grant' among the wire mutations answered Failed{S10: frozen}, and in the same rule says 'Server-side revocation carries still land'. 6.3 defines the legacy shrink Grant as performing 'the server-side revocation above'. Under the first reading rung 2 of the ladder is unavailable during a ceremony and a service admin's only removal is RemoveIdentity (deregistering the key everywhere); under the second the frozen flag does not hold a shrink Grant. 13 tests 'S10 refuses ... legacy Grant' and 'not the revocation carry', which is consistent only if 'legacy Grant' there means the additive/idempotent forms.
findings.fix: S10: 'legacy Grant that is not a strict-subset shrink'; add 'a legacy shrink Grant lands on a frozen group like RemoveIdentity (its carry is a server-side revocation)'.

findings.section: 10 'The k8s operator' (pins Secret on HeadAccepted, resetPins one-shot) / P4 rewind rule
findings.title: The pins Secret can lag the mirror (broadcast Lagged, failed patch, unreported), and resetPins re-applies on every boot while set
findings.detail: The operator writes group_pin rows to the Secret 'on every HeadAccepted'. ReplicaEvent is a broadcast channel of capacity 1024 (src/replica.rs EVENTS_CAPACITY) and a rotation emits SecretChanged per secret per group at once (section 10 calls it a storm); a subscriber that observes Lagged (events.rs already handles it by re-triggering reconciles) loses the HeadAccepted for that head, and a failed Secret patch (API down, quota) is not surfaced. The mirror is an emptyDir, so after the next pod restart the replica boots with a pin at head n-k while it had served head n: P4 accepts any node at or above n-k, so a rewound or stale authoritative node (the residual 7.4 bounds by 'pins bound rollback') is accepted for k heads, and a reader kicked in those heads is re-authorized by the mirror. resetPins is 'one-shot' but is a chart value the operator reads at every boot: while it remains set, every restart resets the pin to the genesis and accepts any chain from it.
findings.fix: Write the Secret from Replica::pins() (the whole table) on every HeadAccepted and on Lagged, plus on a timer; publish Ready=False/PinsNotPersisted on affected BunkerSecrets when the patch fails until it succeeds. Record applied resets in the Secret (name -> genesis hash) and apply resetPins only when the recorded value differs.

findings.section: 6.1 escalation ladder / 6.3 RemoveIdentity (last service admin) / 11 `db remove-identity`
findings.title: A rogue sole service admin is unreachable by rungs 3 and 4 and the ladder does not name the offline path
findings.detail: RemoveIdentity refuses 'the last service admin' (src/server.rs:544-552, kept by 6.3), SetServiceAdmin and FreezeGroup are service-admin-only. Sequence: rogue service admin S removes every other service admin (allowed while not last) and holds admin rows on groups. Rung 2 needs a requester who is an admin (S is the only one); rung 3 cannot remove S; rung 4's freeze can only be set by S, and a recovery without a freeze against an online S that churns is the case the freeze exists for. The path that works is offline (`db remove-identity` with carries per the S7 finding, then a recovery), which 11 lists for migration only.
findings.fix: Add rung (5) to 6.1 and 7.4: 'service stopped, `db remove-identity --name <rogue>` (authors the carries) and `db set-service-admin`, then restart and recover'; or let RemoveIdentity of the last service admin succeed when the caller is a different identity presenting a backup-signed authorization (out of scope), and say which.
